candidates.title: Prepare phone game-test logs for Sheets

demandEvidence.chore: The post describes logging battery, temperature, frame drops, and session notes during mobile game tests, then transferring exported CSV rows into Google Sheets; it also reports unreliable and duplicate file triggers.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I have tried a Schedule Trigger plus Google Drive Watch Files and also a Webhook from a shortcut on the phone, but the workflow either doesn’t fire at all or fires twice on the same file.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable row for each fictional game-test session, with duplicate files flagged before a person imports it.
inputs: A fictional CSV export with session time and test measurements
A fictional file name and upload-complete flag
An operator-provided list of previously processed file names
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a completed sample export or a new fictional file record.
steps: Read the supplied CSV and preserve its original rows.
Check the file name against the operator-provided processed-file list.
Flag repeated names or incomplete uploads without merging them.
Prepare a proposed spreadsheet-ready row set and an exception note.
Ask a person to verify measurements, resolve flags, and approve any import.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Use two identical fictional file names and one incomplete upload; confirm both are flagged and all unflagged measurement values match the input exactly.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies test files, checks measurements and duplicate flags, and authorizes any real phone, Drive, or Sheets access and import.
unverified: n8n schedule, Drive watch, or webhook execution
Google Sheets writes and duplicate prevention in a live workflow

ease.reason: Fictional CSV parsing and duplicate flag review are approachable; no supplied reference documents the phone or n8n mechanics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent game testers may pay to reduce repeated log transfer; this post establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can preserve rows and flag duplicate files, while phone uploads and live Sheets writes remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed duplicate check can repeat on sample rows, but a person must verify exceptions and approve imports.

evidence.reason: The retained context and task spans describe the repeated log-transfer chore and trigger failures; wider demand and implementation support are absent.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore assessed as a proposed synthetic-data experiment; the provisional mean is below the threshold, so it is not proposed for publication.

experimentPlan.output: A review list of repeated fictional lead-batch items, with the original rows preserved for operator review.
inputs: An operator-provided list of previously processed identifiers
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a completed fictional lead batch for a duplicate review.
steps: Read the supplied batch and retain every original row.
Compare the operator-provided identifiers with prior fictional identifiers.
Flag possible repeats without deleting or merging records.
Produce a review list with the source row references.
Have a person verify flags and choose any production changes.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Feed one fictional batch twice; confirm the second pass flags repeated identifiers and preserves every row for review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person defines identifiers, supplies test batches, verifies match decisions, and approves all production edits.
unverified: Actual lead fields and identifier rules
n8n scheduling and persistent processed-batch storage

ease.reason: A sample batch comparison is approachable, but no attached source documents scheduling or persistent deduplication mechanics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: lead-generation operators may pay to avoid repeated processing; the retained post does not establish buying intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare fictional batches; live lead-source access and persistent state remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A person must supply identifiers, resolve matches, and authorize changes; no execution capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The retained task span names duplicate processing from missed triggers, but fields, recurrence, and corroboration are absent.

candidates.reason: A bounded batch-review experiment is assessable, but the provisional mean is below six and there is no supplied implementation reference.

candidates.title: Review weekly keyword metrics in Sheets

demandEvidence.chore: A weekly workflow runs a keyword search-volume actor and adds search volume, cost-per-click, and difficulty values to Google Sheets.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Runs VNCNT Labs’ Keyword Search Volume Actor on Apify every week and adds each keyword’s Google search volume, CPC and difficulty as rows in Google Sheets.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable weekly keyword table that compares operator-supplied search metrics with the prior sample and flags changes.
inputs: A fictional list of target keywords
A fictional weekly CSV with volume, CPC, and difficulty columns
A prior fictional weekly metrics CSV
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies the latest fictional weekly keyword metrics export.
steps: Check that each input row has a keyword and the three expected metric values.
Match current rows to prior rows by the supplied keyword text.
Calculate proposed differences for matching rows.
Flag missing or malformed values without filling them in.
Prepare a spreadsheet-ready comparison for human review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Use a tiny fictional current and prior CSV with one changed metric and one missing keyword; verify the difference and missing-row flags against hand calculations.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person chooses keywords, obtains metric data, validates calculations, and approves any upload or business interpretation.
unverified: Live Apify actor or Google keyword endpoint execution
Whether a particular professional-services buyer needs this report repeatedly
Accuracy and coverage of supplied keyword metrics

ease.reason: A student can test comparison logic on fictional CSVs, but no supplied source supports running the actor or writing Sheets.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: search consultants may pay for recurring keyword reports; this example shows a workflow but no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week fictional comparison report is bounded; live metrics, endpoint use, and sheet persistence are unverified.

autonomy.reason: Metric comparison can repeat on supplied files, while a person must obtain data and review its meaning; no live loop is supported.

evidence.reason: The retained post describes a weekly metrics-to-Sheets workflow and a stated per-result price, but not independent demand or actual customer use.

candidates.reason: The post supplies a concrete weekly reporting workflow, but the proposed mock has no implementation evidence and its provisional mean is below six.

steps.message: Assessed all nine sealed discussion identities. Three concrete reporting or duplicate-review tasks received scoped experiments and provisional five-criterion scores; each mean is below six. The remaining posts lack a concrete supported chore, are a one-off trigger bug, or repeat the published support-inbox workflow. No post is proposed.
